correctness.rationale: For every n >= 2, matching-edge distance is 1-[k=j] and same-layer horizontal-edge distance is 1-[k in X]+[b!=a]. Matching edges force at least n-1 occupied columns. With exactly n-1 selected vertices, an omitted column and one landmark per other column are forced; explicit indistinguishable rung/horizontal pairs exclude any side with fewer than three landmarks. Conversely four exhaustive edge-type comparisons distinguish every edge pair if both sides have at least three. Entire clique layer always resolves, giving n for n <= 6 and n-1 for n >= 7. Three clique-layer slides exchange opposite-layer column occupants at fixed hole; horizontal hole relocation and legal vertical flips connect all admissible populations. The direct program exhausts graph instances n=2..9; the second independently checks enumeration and slide connectivity n=7..10. Both were executed and their outputs match the recorded files. Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The complete prism has a known mixed metric minimum n and n-vertex transversal bases, but mixed resolving distinguishes vertices and edges; the present edge-only minimum n-1 (n>=7), exact n-1 basis classification/count, and connected token-slide network do not follow from that stronger metric condition. The original edge metric paper treats several families but not this precise theorem; Zubrilina proves a generic k-to-k+1 interval for products with paths, not all exact bases and slides. Actual public record, own historical archive and literature searches found no duplicate, with acknowledged priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The seven-column threshold reveals when a complete-clique prism first permits omitting one landmark while distinguishing every edge, and the classification enumerates every optimum set for an infinite family. The constructive connectedness theorem guarantees mobility under the more restrictive adjacency-only replacement model, rather than merely arbitrary jumps. These structural, counting and dynamical facts have a natural reason for this graph family and are not implied by the already known mixed minimum.
